record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does the class of asymptotically flat 3-manifolds satisfying the hypotheses of the positive mass theorem have a weak compactness property, such as subsequential convergence for sequences with bounded mass and bounded geometry, and what regularity should the limiting manifold have?

evidence.quote: Show the set 'f 'JTI, of AF 3-manifolds which satisfy the conditions of the positive mass theorem [SY1,2;WE] has some weak compactness property, eg. a sequence {Mk} with bounded mass and bounded geometry has a convergent subsequence (cf. [0M2] and these proceedings). What regularity might we expect in the limit manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complete Riemannian 3-manifold $(M,g)$ is called asymptotically flat (AF) if there is a compact set $K\subset M$ such that $M\setminus K$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\setminus B$ for some closed ball $B$, and in the induced asymptotic coordinates the metric satisfies
$$g_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+O(|x|^{-1}),\quad \partial g_{ij}=O(|x|^{-2}),\quad \partial^2 g_{ij}=O(|x|^{-3}),$$
with scalar curvature $R_g\in L^1(M)$ and $R_g\ge 0$. The ADM mass of such an end is
$$m(g)=\frac{1}{16\pi}\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}\sum_{i,j}(\partial_i g_{ij}-\partial_j g_{ii})\,\nu^j\,dA.$$
Let $\mathcal{M}$ denote the class of such AF 3-manifolds (with nonnegative scalar curvature, so that the positive mass theorem applies giving $m(g)\ge 0$).

Say a sequence $\{(M_k,g_k)\}\subset\mathcal{M}$ has bounded geometry if there are uniform bounds on injectivity radius from below and on sectional curvature, and bounded mass if $\sup_k m(g_k)<\infty$.

Problem: Does $\mathcal{M}$ admit a weak compactness property? Concretely, does every sequence $\{(M_k,g_k)\}\subset\mathcal{M}$ with bounded mass and bounded geometry admit a subsequence converging (in a suitable pointed topology such as pointed $C^{1,\alpha}$, Lipschitz, Gromov–Hausdorff, or measured Gromov–Hausdorff sense) to a limit space $(M_\infty,g_\infty)$? What is the optimal regularity of such a limit, and to what extent does it remain an AF manifold satisfying the hypotheses of the positive mass theorem?
artifact.category_tag: Asymptotically flat manifolds and positive mass theorem
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on compactness/stability questions for AF 3-manifolds related to the positive mass theorem. In particular, stability results show that AF 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and ADM mass tending to zero converge (under various assumptions) to Euclidean 3-space, e.g. in pointed measured Gromov–Hausdorff topology (Dong–Song, Invent. Math. 2024), and effective/quantitative versions have been established (Lee–Sormani and others). However, the general weak-compactness question for sequences with bounded (not necessarily small) mass and bounded geometry, together with the precise regularity of the limit, remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Euclidean 3-space for the positive mass theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Given a sequence of complete asymptotically flat 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature where the ADM mass converges to 0, the manifolds converge to R^3 in the pointed measured Gromov-Hausdorff topology.
status_evidence.claim: Partial compactness/stability is known when masses tend to zero.

status_evidence.title: Effective versions of the positive mass theorem
status_evidence.snippet: For asymptotically flat 3-manifolds with horizon boundary and nonnegative scalar curvature, effective versions of the positive mass theorem are obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative/effective forms exist but a full weak compactness theorem with general bounded mass is not established.
